utterances.text: If you want to blow it up even more, we can. Do you want to blow it even up more, sir?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: I just want to make sure we're talking about same school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, [sic], that area around C, if we could blow that up a little more.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: I did not know that there was a mortar location at that school, if that's what your question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, I take it, when you were driving around with Mr. Dreyer and looking around, you never saw any ARSK mortar locations?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: No. Mr. Dreyer assumed the 50-cal round, so he was mostly out of the building - out of the building - out of the APC. I was firmly inside the APC. I had the main hatch open on the inside, so we could see some objects. He would have had a much better vantage point than I would, while driving.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to the photograph of the school, which is 982.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dreyer [sic], this particular school, this is a large building relative to the rest of the buildings in Knin, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: You referring to me as "Mr. Dreyer" again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I am sorry. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... complex. Say again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This building that you've identified as the -- that was totally destroyed, this is a relatively large building in Knin vis-a-vis the rest of the buildings in the town, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: Correct. It is a substantial structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you continued to drive around Knin after the 6th of August until the time you actually departed, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you two items.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: One is D276, If we could just play this briefly. No sound is required, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Stop right there. Just go back up a little bit. Stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dreyer, [sic], what you are talking about is the structure on the left-hand side of this photograph about midway through. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, excuse me. Mr. Dawes.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: I'm flattered. He's much more handsome than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: He is, at that. Mr. Dawes, that is the building you're talk about?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: I can't really tell, but it is definitely in the general area, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, that general building appears to have no destruction on the roof, does it?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, let us move to another document -- item.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 1D57-0094. This is a clip from Zastava Films received from the Prosecution. There again is no sound, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is an item from Zastava Films which is part of the RSK taken on the 4th of August, 1995, Mr. Dawes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could play this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, again, Mr. Dawes, this is the building that you are talking about, that someone told you was totally destroyed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: If I -- no disrespect, if you take you at its word, then that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'll offer into evidence 1D57-0097 -- 94, excuse me, 0094.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no objection to the admission. I want to be clear, the video that was -- that he indicated was the video sent over by the Prosecution, that video had sound. I don't know if this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was played just for the purpose of identifying the building for which you do not need the sound. That's what I understood, and I think that was already in evidence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just -- we received the bulk of it, and I think both sides have cut parts out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: In any case, no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D861.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D861 is admitted into evidence. Now, Mr. Kehoe, one of the things I asked myself is that this witness testified that someone told him that the school was destroyed, and that he had never seen it. What is the purpose? I mean, if you show this is to us and say this the building, the witness can't confirm that. What is there what we learned from this witness over the last four to five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will -- I will -- first of all, it's on the 4th, but it takes me to the next point -- to go to the next point given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, we'll see. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dawes, you stated that you didn't know who told you that the building was totally destroyed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, as you sit here, whoever told you that, you know that person was exaggerating the extent of destruction on this building, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: If that was the building, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: During the course of your time there, sir, were many of the reports that you received about damage in Knin exaggerated by UN personnel?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. We've heard no testimony regarding reports received by this witness concerning anything, much less damage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we should first establish that; but even then, I do understand that the witness had two days after beginning of Operation Storm, that the school was destroyed. You show us now, I think, pictures from the 4th and the 5th of August, which leaves --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The 4th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I thought one of them was the 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The 5th is the first one in evidence ... [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... okay. The witness tell us, "I do not know." So whether someone exaggerates or not, he couldn't know either. What you are doing is you are asking this witness to draw a lot of conclusions on the basis of material where he has no personal observation, just to lead him to the place that everyone exaggerated, which could not be a conclusion - it may well be - that everyone exaggerated, but you cannot establish that on the basis of this material. If it's from a witness about if this is the school, if this is the total destruction, then that person must have exaggerated, I don't need a witness to understand that. And, certainly, Mr. Dawes is very much assisting and being very precise and said If someone said it was totally destroyed and if this is the building which appears to not be totally destroyed, then he must have exaggerated, not even knowing whether this was the state of the building on the 4th, the 5th, the 6th. Apparently, he learned about it on the 6th and not on the 4th or the 5th. So, therefore, I do not understand your techniques, apparent --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I need to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...trial techniques, which --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I can explain my technique, Judge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not in the presence of the witness. I am just point to you that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Judge, I understand the technique and the greater plan outside the presence of the witness at any time because there is a string that, not only is with this witness but with other witnesses, when we do put these facts together will become abundantly clear to Your Honour. So cross-examination is not just with this particular fact and circumstance concerning certainly this exaggeration fact which we've heard a lot of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My certain is that we're putting all these facts together; whereas, the whole exaggeration issue, at least as far as this school is concerned, as I pointed to you now, is not a fact, and that is exactly at least not an established fact. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, just talking about the hospital trip, and moving away from this, it is accurate to say that when you went to the hospital, you never got out of the APC. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: That is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: I don't remember either way. We were dropping the doctor off, if that's the trip you're talking where we took the doctor to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On page --

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: Page 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- or P981, you told the Prosecution on the 2nd ever April, 2008, at paragraph 15: "I did not ..." -- second line: "I did not go into the hospital or get out of the APC."

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: All right. I was just looking at my testimony from 1996. Sorry, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So that -- is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: Then that is accurate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So anything that you learned about what happened to the hospital, you got from third parties and you didn't observe yourself. Right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's briefly talk about the barracks. You noted during the statement, on page 4 of your 1996 statement, that you passed -- "when we passed close to the northern barracks, I saw no impacts there." Is it your testimony that there were no impacts at the northern barracks or you just didn't see them?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: I am saying that while I drove by the northern barracks, I did not see any impacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, if you were seated in the bottom of the APC and driving passed the northern barracks, how did you see that there were no impacts?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: Well, you're standing on a bench in the APC and you were looking out through the main hatch, so you have horizontal vision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me be clear: Number one, you didn't go into the northern barracks; right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Number two, we are talking about impacts or information that you get driving passed on the road, right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not here to educate you, Mr. Dawes, but if the RSK reported impacts at the northern barracks on the morning of the 4th of August, you have no reason to question that, do you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was first waiting for the French translation. The witness testified in what position he was and that he did not see any impacts, then whether he had reason -- of course, unless there's any specific, I do expect what that what he didn't see, that he has no reason to believe that something may have been there or not have been there if he was not in a position to see it. That's how I and I think the Bench will understand his testimony. Now, if you want to establish that there were impacts, fine; but, then, preferably with a witness who inspected the northern barracks or who gives a different position as from where he observed matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, that calls into question the methodology of the Prosecutor to lead this type of evidence, because Prosecution knows full well that there are documents in evidence from the RSK reflecting artillery fire in the northern barracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But this witness testifies about what he knows, and in relation to this, he said "I didn't see this," which doesn't say that it wasn't there. It's just that this witness is -- that's what he tells us; and if there's any --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Then why lead that evidence, Judge? Why lead that evidence, unless the Prosecution wants the Chamber to believe that the northern barracks weren't shelled, when, in fact, they were? That's the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are not going to discuss through the testimony this witness what the Prosecution does and $does not. We have in front of us now this witness who gave his statement, and which appears the line that he did not see any impact. If you want to criticize the leading of this evidence, of course, you can do it, but why bother this witness with --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Frankly, Your Honour, I would think that Your Honour would question how the OTP is presenting this, given the fact that the are leading evidence that I have to respond to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take that the Prosecution will tell us that we have to look at their evidence in its totality as well, in which this is only a tiny little thing of someone who did not see something. And where it may have been there or not been there, I do not know; but at least this witness didn't see it. That's, of course, the weight to not observing a matter is rather limited. Let's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Russo. And let's not spend so time in relation to this witness, because this witness will not be able to respond, unless there are any specific to believe that he can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, with all due respect, the Prosecution led this specific item of evidence with Mr. Dawes about impacts in the northern barracks, clearly trying to bring it to the Chamber 's attention that there was no shelling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is argumentative, rather than eliciting from a witness knowledge of what he observed, what he have seen. And if you want to criticize the Prosecution for that, again let's not bother the witness with it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, then, on the next step, may I be permitted to show him a document concerning the actual shelling of that, albeit he has not seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why? Unless you have any reason that, when looking at this, he would say, "Oh, well, of course, that is what I saw the day after that or the day before that." But this witness -- Let's not, as again I said, educate witnesses. If you want to put something to a witness in contradiction to what he said, then there should be a reasonable expectation that this would further assist him in his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, Mr. Russo has been on his feet for a while ... [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I know he tires easy -- or "easily" is probably the correct adverb.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to -- I understand the Court's position with respect to this particular witness, but I would like to make an objection to the discussion of evidence led by the Prosecution in the presence of a witness. I believe this Court is more interested in what each particular witness has observed outside of the influence of other evidence that other witnesses provided at least in the first instances. So I don't think it is appropriate to be discussing the what the Prosecution led, why they didn't lead it, in the presence of this witness, and I would just like to make that point, so it doesn't happen in front of another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are items that are in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed. I think it is clear what I earlier said about showing a picture to the witness. Whether the witness should see it or whether we should see it is not the same. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dawes, during the course of your driving around on the 4th, you informed Mr. Stanton that there was definitely outgoing artillery fire from Serb locations in Knin on the 4th. Where were those locations where you either heard or observed outgoing Serb artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: I was told that by somebody. I can't remember the individual's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would that have been an UN soldier who told you that there was outgoing Serb artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: No idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Assuming that person told you that, did he say where it was from?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, staying with your trip on the -- your first trip, and if I could just talk a little bit about your trip where you observed -- or the opportunity to see the cluster bomblets. You noted for us, during the course of your testimony that the -- or during the course of your -- this is page 5 in the 1996 statement, where the tree tops had been cut off. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And let me show you a film, which is again part of the Zastava Films.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 1D57-0095. Yes. I have just been informed there is again no sound on this, if we can play this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dawes, does that appear to be the location that you were talking about where the trees had been cut off?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: No idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You can observe, looking at that pavement, that there are no bomblets on that pavement, or that you can observe, are there?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'll offer 1D57-0095 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D861 -- sorry, D862, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D862 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can go back to P62, just a blank sheet, and that would be P62. It should be the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Aerial view on Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Looking at P62, if I can turn your attention to page 5 of P980, at the top of the page: "During the trip, we kept the tops down on the -- top open on the APC to be able to look for UN personnel. When we passed, about 150 metres south of the main crossing in the centre of Knin going in the direction towards the bus station, we suddenly discovered that most of the tree tops along the alley-way were cut; however, not too much damages was seen ..." I'm reading it literally: "... however, not too much damages was seen at the bottom of those trees. We then saw the bomblets, some small bombs from a cluster bomb. Both Andries and I looked at these and at each other, and I remember that we were commenting that we should stay away from the bomblets." In the statement that you made in 1996, where on this map did you place these bomblets 150 metres south from the main crossing in the centre going in the direction of the bus station? Where did you put them?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: Is the blue pen ready again? In that general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me flip back to -- your 1996 statement, that's where you put them?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: Well, that's where I recollect --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, no, no, sir --

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: -- them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Stay with me here.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: I'm trying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You noted for us this morning that your memory back in 1996 about these events was much better than in 2008. And when you gave this statement in 1996, where, based on this statement at the top of page 5, did you put the location of those bomblets that you allegedly saw? If I can give you a frame of reference --

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go back to P984, and you can pinpoint the bus station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I'm looking at the clock, and it seems that you are engaging in a most complex exercise. Perhaps we should not do it at this moment. It's a quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's fine, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, we'll soon adjourn for the day, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow mourning in this same courtroom. Madam Usher, could you already escort Mr. Dawes out of the courtroom -- Oh, Mr. Dawes, one second, please. I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether the portion already given or the portion still to be given tomorrow, so you should refrain from any conversation about your testimony. Yes. Could you then please follow Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, usual question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will finish, Your Honour, at the end of the second session tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as of now, I have no questions. That may change, but, likely, I will have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider -- we had some discussions about -- well, not discussions perhaps. I made some comments in relation to the way in which you conducted the cross-examination, what would assist us and what would not assist us. The Chamber will briefly discuss this and see whether, then, it will allow you the two full sessions tomorrow you are asking for. We will adjourn, and we will resume tomorrow, the 14th of October, at 9.00 in Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 14th day of October, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 25
